Implement a mechanism to detect and report idle server processes in Accumulo clusters, and enable custom tagging of metrics for better observability. Ensure that server processes emit an idle metric after a configurable idle period and support custom key-value tags on all metrics.

*   Define a constant `METRICS_SERVER_IDLE` with the value `'accumulo.server.idle'` in the `MetricsProducer` interface located at `core/src/main/java/org/apache/accumulo/core/metrics/MetricsProducer.java`.
*   Add configuration properties to the `Property` enum in `core/src/main/java/org/apache/accumulo/core/conf/Property.java`:
    *   `GENERAL_IDLE_PROCESS_INTERVAL` with the key `'general.metrics.process.idle'` to specify the idle duration before emitting the idle metric. It should accept time duration values.
    *   `GENERAL_MICROMETER_USER_TAGS` with the key `'general.micrometer.user.tags'` to accept a comma-separated list of 'key=value' pairs for tagging metrics.
*   Ensure all metrics emitted by server processes include a `process.name` tag:
    *   Use `'tserver'` for tablet servers.
    *   Use `'sserver'` for scan servers.
    *   Use `'compactor'` for compactors.
*   Implement the emission of the `accumulo.server.idle` metric for tablet servers, scan servers, and compactors when they have been idle for the duration specified by `GENERAL_IDLE_PROCESS_INTERVAL`. Tag these metrics with the appropriate `process.name`.
*   Ensure the `accumulo.server.idle` metric is not emitted during normal active operations.
*   When `GENERAL_MICROMETER_USER_TAGS` is configured, append the specified tags to all metrics emitted by server processes.

**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

Here's what I found about the Apache Accumulo `accumulo.server.idle` metric and the `updateIdleStatus` method, based on the search results.

## The `accumulo.server.idle` Metric

The metric originated in PR #4078, which added it to the elasticity branch. The commit added a counter that is incremented when the server process is idle for the duration specified by the property general.metrics.process.idle. This work touched files including `AbstractServer.java`, `ProcessMetrics.java`, `Compactor.java`, `ScanServer.java`, and `TabletServer.java`.

The metric's definition was later normalized. As of the current metric definitions, `SERVER_IDLE("accumulo.server.idle", MetricType.GAUGE`, "Indicates if the server is idle or not. The value will be 1 when idle and 0 when not idle."

## The `updateIdleStatus` Rename (PR #4740)

The `updateIdleStatus` method was introduced through a refactoring in PR #4740. According to the PR description, several changes were made:

- `AbstractServer.updateIdleStatus()` was changed from having `Supplier<Boolean>` as its input to just a `boolean`. This was done to simplify things since the method was just using it as a boolean anyways, and the method was also renamed from `idleProcessCheck()` to `updateIdleStatus()`.
- The idle check in `Compactor` was simplified to just set the idle status to true or false during its operation. This removes duplicate logic that checks it has been idle for a period of time, and adds test cases to ensure that the idle metric for Compactor and ScanServer behave as expected.

The related PR #4737/#4740 explains the rationale for simplifying the Compactor's idle check: the new code just returns true when no compaction is running and false when one is, deferring the time checking portion to the upstream logic in `AbstractServer`. The old method was to check how much time has passed since the last compaction was completed. One of the identified issues was that there was a check that the `System.nanoTime()` value of the last completed compaction is not negative, which is not a safe check to make since `System.nanoTime()` may provide a negative value.

## Backport to 2.1 (PR #4716)

The metric was backported to the 2.1 branch. PR #4716 backported changes from idle stop PR #4078, converted the idle metric from Counter to Gauge, and removed the COMPACTOR_BUSY metric as a duplicate of this one. During review, there was discussion that the property description needed updating: since the metric became a gauge, the suggested description was "Amount of time a process must be idle before the accumulo.server.idle metric emits the value 1. At other times this metric reports 0."

## How `updateIdleStatus` Is Used

In practice, the servers call `updateIdleStatus` with a boolean reflecting their busy/idle state. For example, in the Compactor, the code marks the compactor as idle (`updateIdleStatus(true)`) while not in the compaction loop, and marks it as busy (`updateIdleStatus(false)`) while compacting. In the ScanServer, the status was updated based on whether the active scans list was empty and the tablet metadata cache estimated size was zero.

## A Caveat on Using This Metric

One important nuance came up in PR #5074 discussion: using the server idle metric to gauge whether or not the Compactor is running a compaction is probably not the way to go, because the process has to be idle for a period of time, regulated by `Property.GENERAL_IDLE_PROCESS_INTERVAL`, to be considered idle.

Most recently, this code was touched again in PR #5811. The commit "Fixes for process exit, added ExitCodesIT (#5811)" made various changes to clean up the exit process of the server processes and added ExitCodesIT to confirm exit codes under different conditions.

You can view the full details at the linked GitHub PRs (#4078, #4716, #4737/#4740, #5811) if you need the complete diffs.
